entries.test: Public evaluations of the relevant LLMs' data requirements, interpretability, reasoning, hallucinations and representations of unfolding events would test the stated limitations.
entries.note: The proposition removes the 2019/GPT-2 framing and turns a prospective inadequacy claim into an unqualified present-tense assertion.

entries.test: Published evaluations of contemporary architectures on commonsense and physical reasoning, including tasks requiring world models, would test the claimed architectural shortcomings.
entries.note: “Essential to AI” broadens the contextual claim into a requirement for AI generally. The passage nevertheless makes an empirical claim about current architectures.

entries.test: Public evaluations of LLMs trained without dedicated commonsense, physical-reasoning or world-model mechanisms would show whether those capabilities arise from ordinary language-model training.
entries.note: In context, “for free” means without specific architectural or training provisions for these capabilities. Marcus explicitly identifies this as his own longstanding position.
This is a prescription for model design without a specified performance goal against which necessity could be tested.
The proposition turns explicitly speculative conjectures about importance into unqualified design recommendations. Listing speculation as a condition does not preserve that hedge in the proposition.

entries.test: Published architecture descriptions and benchmark results for AlphaGeometry and other cited neurosymbolic systems would establish whether they achieved substantial demonstrated performance.
entries.note: The named example gives “strong results” a concrete empirical reference.
The source identifies Marcus and LeCun and includes understanding what to do next; the proposition drops both. “Fully understand” and the population whose minority is meant lack a shared public test.
